summary: Round-3 delta verification: all 3 P3 fixes VERIFIED and the 5 REGRESSION checkpoints all PASS. Details: (1) XFF revert — server.py:103-115 `_client_ip_key` returns `hops[len - TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS]` = rightmost for N=1; all 5 TestClientIpKey unit tests pass in isolation (0.43s). This is the standard XFF interpretation and closes SEC-005 raised in iteration_6. (2) Address IDOR — PATCH /api/addresses/{A_B.id} with customer1's JWT returns 404 (not 200 with leaked doc); customer1's GET /api/addresses does NOT include A_B. (3) forgot-password enumeration — POST identifier=owner AND POST identifier=nobody@nowhere.example both return exactly `{"message": "If the account exists, recovery instructions were sent"}`; the unknown-account body has no `channel`, `reset_token`, or `dev_otp` keys; both `message` strings are byte-identical so an attacker cannot enumerate. Regression: owner/tech1/customer1 logins all return 200 with access_token; `active=True` on fresh registrations; customer1 booking flow works end-to-end (service catalog list → address selection → POST /api/bookings 200 → GET /api/bookings/{id} returns matching address_id); quotation happy path works (create → response has token+public_url; GET /api/quotations/{id} strips token; POST /send rotates token so old public_url 404s and new works). Suite runs: test_security_hardening.py 20/20 PASS in isolation (8.15s after 65s wait for slowapi buckets); test_security_hardening_v2.py 9/10 PASS with 1 skipped and 1 rate-limit-collision failure on TestLegitimateFlow (verify-otp 10/min bucket consumed by preceding TestVerifyOtpRateLimit); TestLegitimateFlow PASSES in isolation. This is the exact test-infra limitation flagged in the review request — not a product bug. New file /app/backend/tests/test_round3_deltas.py exercises the 3 P3 deltas + all regression checkpoints: 10/10 PASS in 5.52s. Notes for main agent: (a) `+919999900802` from the review spec is already registered in this preview; my test picks a random fresh mobile so it works idempotently. (b) customer1's seeded addresses currently both have is_default=false — I don't consider that a regression from the deltas (the 'DEFAULT' UI badge / auto-populate is best-effort in the current data; the booking POST still succeeds with any user-owned address). Flagging as a minor seed hygiene issue for main agent.

minor.issue: Both seeded addresses for customer1 (Home and Office) have is_default=false in the DB. The review request assumed 'Home · DEFAULT' auto-populates. Booking POST still works with any owned address, so this is cosmetic — but the frontend badge/auto-select code will silently pick the first address instead of the intended default. Fix: seed script should set is_default=True on the Home address (or run `db.addresses.updateOne({label:'Home', user_id:<customer1.id>}, {$set:{is_default:true}})`).

critical_code_review_comments: server.py:103-115 `_client_ip_key` — CORRECT. Rightmost XFF entry for N=1 is standard semantics (proxy-appended, forge-proof). Iteration_6 mistakenly asserted the opposite; that recommendation was rejected and reverted.
server.py:801-810 `update_address` — CORRECT. Owner-scoped update_one + matched_count==0 → 404, and the follow-up read is also owner-scoped. No IDOR leak in the error body.

server.py:634-671 `forgot` — CORRECT. Response `message` is the SAME generic string for both unknown-user and real-user paths; DEV_MODE only APPENDS `channel`, `reset_token`, and optionally `dev_otp`. The unknown branch returns bare `generic` so no metadata is emitted.
